picks.headline: AI-informed AdaptiveFlow redefines large-scale cloud computing for drug discovery
picks.rationale: St. Jude/Harvard's AdaptiveFlow screens billions of drug-like molecules at ~1,000x lower compute cost than existing ultra-large screening methods — a concrete, quantified AI-for-science advance.
picks.excerpt: Scientists from St. Jude, the University of Pavia, Dana-Farber and Harvard unveiled AdaptiveFlow, an AI-informed platform that can virtually screen billions of drug-like molecules at roughly 1,000-fold lower computational cost than existing ultra-large screening methods.

picks.headline: AI-driven polymer discovery could replace years of trial and error with closed-loop testing
picks.rationale: Proposes a closed-loop ecosystem linking databases, predictive models, AI agents, simulations and automated labs — a template for how materials-science R&D pipelines are being restructured around AI.
picks.excerpt: Researchers propose a closed-loop polymer-discovery ecosystem that links databases, predictive models, AI agents, simulations and automated labs to compress years of trial-and-error materials work into much faster cycles.

picks.headline: Live from ICM 2026: What Is Math For in the Age of AI?
picks.rationale: A live dispatch from the International Congress of Mathematicians on what mathematicians still value about doing math as AI systems increasingly generate proofs — high-credibility reflection on AI's frontier in a rigorous discipline.
picks.excerpt: A live recording from the International Congress of Mathematicians examines what mathematicians value about doing math as AI systems increasingly generate proofs and tackle open problems.

picks.headline: In an Age of AI, a Physicist Seeks What Endures
picks.rationale: Yale physicist Sarah Demers is drafting an APS policy statement on AI, weighing real risks against benefits like an AI system already helping control the Mu2e experiment — a credible, policy-relevant angle on AI in physics.
picks.excerpt: Yale physicist Sarah Demers, who is drafting an American Physical Society policy statement on AI, weighs the technology's risks against emerging benefits, including an AI system that helps control the Mu2e experiment's search for a rare muon-to-electron transformation.

picks.headline: Brain-Computer Interface Aligns Better with Humans via AI
picks.rationale: New research shows combining human motor learning with AI improves BCI calibration and performance — a novel result with direct relevance to people who've lost the ability to move or speak, rounding out the section with cognitive-science coverage.
picks.excerpt: New research shows that combining human motor learning with AI improves brain-computer interface calibration and performance, offering hope for people who have lost the ability to move or speak.
